1. Course Overview

The CWC Assistant Manager – Technical Post is a comprehensive 40‑hour program designed to equip aspiring technical managers with the knowledge, skills, and practical tools required to lead engineering teams, oversee project delivery, and drive continuous improvement in a construction‑focused environment.

Tip

Read the entire syllabus before enrolling to ensure the course aligns with your career goals.

Key themes include:

  • Technical leadership fundamentals
  • Project planning, risk, and cost control
  • Quality assurance & health‑safety compliance
  • Data‑driven decision making
  • People management and stakeholder communication

2. Learning Outcomes

Upon successful completion, participants will be able to:

  1. Interpret technical specifications and translate them into actionable work plans.
  2. Develop realistic project schedules using critical‑path methodology.
  3. Apply cost‑control techniques to keep projects within budget.
  4. Implement quality‑control procedures that meet CWC standards.
  5. Lead multidisciplinary teams, fostering collaboration and accountability.
  6. Utilise digital tools (BIM, project dashboards) for monitoring progress.
  7. Prepare clear, concise reports for senior management and clients.

3. Target Audience & Prerequisites

This syllabus is intended for:

  • Site engineers and senior technicians aspiring to move into management.
  • Current assistant managers seeking formal certification.
  • Project coordinators who need a deeper technical grounding.

Prerequisites

  • Minimum 2 years of hands‑on experience in construction or civil engineering.
  • Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with CAD/BIM concepts.
  • English language proficiency (reading technical documents).

Warning

Participants lacking the minimum experience may struggle with advanced case studies.

4. Course Structure & Modules

Each module builds on the previous one; mastery of early concepts (e.g., scheduling) is essential for later topics such as cost control and digital analytics.

5. Teaching Methods

The course uses a blended learning approach:

  • Interactive Lectures: 30 % – theory and best‑practice frameworks.
  • Hands‑On Labs: 25 % – software tools (MS Project, Power BI, BIM 360).
  • Case Studies: 20 % – real CWC projects, focusing on problem solving.
  • Group Work: 15 % – collaborative planning, risk workshops.
  • Reflective Debrief: 10 % – personal action‑plan development.

6. Assessment & Certification

Participants are assessed through a combination of formative and summative tasks:

Assessment TypeWeightDetails
In‑class quizzes15 %Short MCQs after each module.
Practical lab assignments35 %Schedule creation, cost‑control spreadsheet, BIM model review.
Group project (Capstone)30 %Develop a full project plan for a hypothetical CWC site.
Final written exam20 %Open‑book, 2‑hour, covering all learning outcomes.

To receive the CWC Assistant Manager – Technical Post Certificate, learners must achieve an overall score of at least 70 % and demonstrate competency in the capstone project.

7. Resources & References

All participants receive a digital learning pack containing:

  • Course handbook (PDF, 120 pages)
  • Template library (WBS, risk register, cost control sheets)
  • Access to a sandbox MS Project and Power BI environment
  • Recommended reading list:
    • PMBOK® Guide – Sixth Edition
    • “Construction Management: Principles and Practice” – Alan Griffith
    • “BIM Handbook” – Chuck Eastman et al.
    • CWC Technical Standards (latest edition)

Key Resource

The CWC Technical Standards document is mandatory reading; exam questions are drawn directly from its clauses.

9. Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a laptop?

Yes. A laptop capable of running Windows 10/11 with at least 8 GB RAM is required for the software labs.

Is there any travel cost?

The course is delivered on‑site at the CWC Training Centre; travel and accommodation are the participant’s responsibility.

Can I retake the exam if I fail?

Yes. A single retake is allowed within 30 days of the original exam date, subject to a nominal fee.

Are there any continuing‑education credits?

Successful graduates receive 15 CPD points recognized by the Institute of Civil Engineers (ICE).

10. Summary & Checklist

Before you begin, confirm the following items to ensure a smooth learning experience:

  • Signed enrollment agreement and payment receipt.
  • Laptop meeting the technical specifications.
  • Printed copy of the CWC Technical Standards (latest edition).
  • Completed pre‑course questionnaire (sent by email).
  • Travel arrangements to the training centre.
  • Personal action‑plan template (provided in the learning pack).

We look forward to supporting your journey toward becoming a proficient Assistant Manager – Technical Post. For any further queries, contact training@cwc.org.
